questions.q: An occupation in which people render personalised services of a specialised nature, based on professional knowledge and training, is called a ______.
questions.e: Doctors, lawyers and chartered accountants follow a profession, which needs specialised knowledge and membership of a professional body.

questions.q: Industries engaged in the extraction and production of natural resources and the reproduction of living organisms are called ______ industries.
questions.e: Primary industries include extractive industries (mining, fishing) and genetic industries (poultry, nurseries).

questions.q: Which objective of business means producing more output with the given resources, and is essential for its survival and growth?
questions.e: Productivity is the ratio of output to input; every business must aim to keep improving it to stay competitive.

questions.q: A rice trader in Karnal stores paddy after harvest and sells it gradually throughout the year. Warehousing here removes the hindrance of ______.
questions.e: Warehousing preserves goods from the time they are produced until they are needed, removing the hindrance of time; transport removes the hindrance of place.

questions.q: Classify the following industries as per the NCERT classification of industries.
p: (a) Coal mining in Jharkhand is which type of primary industry?
extractive|extractive industry
(b) A sugar mill that refines sugarcane belongs to which type of manufacturing industry?
processing|processing industry
(c) A cement factory that combines limestone, clay and gypsum belongs to which type of manufacturing industry?
synthetical|synthetic|synthetical industry
questions.e: Extractive industries take products from natural sources; processing industries put raw material through successive stages (sugar, paper); synthetical industries combine ingredients into a new product (cement, soap).

questions.q: In a Joint Hindu Family business, the eldest member who controls and manages the business is called the ______.
questions.e: The karta manages the family business and has unlimited liability, while the other coparceners have liability limited to their share.

questions.q: The maximum number of members permitted in a private company is ______.
questions.e: Under the Companies Act, 2013, a private company can have at most 200 members (excluding present and past employees).

questions.q: A partner who contributes capital and shares profits but does not take part in the day-to-day running of the firm is a ______ partner.
questions.e: A sleeping or dormant partner is not known to outsiders as active, but still has unlimited liability.

questions.q: Ravi, a famous cricketer, allows a sports-goods firm to use his name as a partner. He invests no capital, takes no share in profits, but is liable to third parties. Ravi is a ______ partner.
questions.e: A nominal partner only lends his name to the firm; he does not contribute capital or share profits, but remains liable to outsiders.

questions.q: A cooperative society formed to provide loans to its members at low rates of interest is a ______ cooperative society.
questions.e: Credit cooperative societies accept deposits and give loans to members at easy terms, protecting them from moneylenders.

questions.q: Meena runs a small boutique in Jaipur all by herself. She takes all decisions alone and keeps the entire profit. If the business fails, creditors can recover their dues from her personal property.
p: (a) Name the form of business organisation.
sole proprietorship|sole proprietor|sole trader|sole proprietary concern|sole proprietary
(b) What is the nature of Meena's liability?
unlimited|unlimited liability
(c) Is the business a separate legal entity from Meena? (yes/no)
no
questions.e: A sole proprietorship is owned and controlled by one person; the owner and business are the same in law, so the owner's liability is unlimited.

questions.q: A government company is one in which not less than ______ percent of the paid-up share capital is held by the government.
questions.e: A government company has at least 51% of its paid-up capital held by the Central and/or State Government(s).

questions.q: Indian Railways and Posts and Telegraphs are examples of ______ undertakings.
questions.e: Departmental undertakings are run as departments of a ministry and are financed by annual budget appropriations.

questions.q: A public enterprise created by a special Act of Parliament or a State Legislature, which defines its powers and functions, is called a ______.
questions.e: Statutory corporations like LIC are set up under a special Act and enjoy the power of government along with the flexibility of private enterprise.

questions.q: Huge business enterprises that have operations in several countries but are controlled from a headquarters in one country are called global enterprises or ______.
questions.a: multinational corporations|multinational corporation|mncs|mnc|multinational companies|multinational company|transnational corporations
questions.e: Global enterprises or MNCs have huge capital, advanced technology and a worldwide network of operations.

questions.q: An Indian auto-parts firm and a Japanese company pool their resources to form a new company in India, sharing ownership, control, profits and risks. This arrangement is a ______.
questions.e: A joint venture is formed when two or more businesses agree to pool resources for a common purpose and share ownership and control.

questions.q: The insurance principle that requires both parties to disclose all material facts honestly is the principle of utmost good ______.
questions.e: Uberrimae fidei (utmost good faith) means the insured must disclose all material facts, otherwise the contract can be avoided.

questions.q: Under the principle of ______, the insured is only compensated for the actual loss suffered and cannot make a profit from insurance.
questions.e: Indemnity applies to fire and marine insurance: the insurer puts the insured back in the position he was in before the loss, not better.

questions.q: Arjun's insured car is damaged by a truck driven carelessly. After the insurance company compensates Arjun, it gets his right to recover damages from the truck owner. Which principle of insurance applies?
questions.e: Under subrogation, after paying the claim the insurer steps into the shoes of the insured and acquires his rights against third parties.

questions.q: The electronic fund transfer system used for transferring large amounts instantly, on a transaction-by-transaction basis, is called ______.
questions.e: RTGS (Real Time Gross Settlement) settles each transaction individually and instantly, and is meant for high-value transfers.

questions.q: Raghav, a basmati rice exporter in Punjab, stores his stock in a warehouse of the Central Warehousing Corporation and insures the stock against fire.
p: (a) A warehouse owned and managed by the Central Warehousing Corporation is which type of warehouse?
government warehouse|government|government warehouses
(b) Which type of insurance has Raghav taken?
fire insurance|fire
(c) To claim, the fire must be the nearest cause of the loss. Name this principle.
causa proxima|proximate cause|principle of causa proxima
questions.e: Government warehouses are owned by central or state governments (e.g., CWC); under causa proxima the insurer pays only if the proximate cause of loss is the insured peril.

questions.q: In online shopping, the payment method in which the buyer pays in cash when the goods are delivered at the doorstep is called ______.
questions.e: Cash on delivery lets buyers who are wary of online payment pay only after receiving the goods.

questions.q: The term for conducting industry, trade and commerce using computer networks, which is wider than e-commerce, is ______.
questions.e: E-business covers all business functions done online (production, finance, HR), while e-commerce covers only buying and selling.

questions.q: Contracting out a firm's non-core activities, such as payroll or customer support, to outside specialist agencies is called ______.
questions.e: Outsourcing lets a firm focus on its core competencies while specialists handle non-core processes.

questions.q: Neha, a college student in Pune, sells her old bicycle to another student through an online classifieds website. This is an example of ______ commerce.
questions.a: c2c|c to c|customer to customer|consumer to consumer|customer-to-customer
questions.e: When one consumer sells to another through a website, the transaction is customer-to-customer (C2C) commerce.

questions.q: ShopKart, an online store, places orders with manufacturers through its website, sells to customers online, and lets its staff apply for leave through the company intranet.
p: (a) Ordering stock from manufacturers online belongs to which category of e-business?
b2b|b to b|business to business|business-to-business
(b) Selling to customers online belongs to which category?
b2c|b to c|business to customer|business to consumer|business-to-customer
(c) Staff applying for leave on the intranet belongs to which category?
intra-b|intra b|intrab|intra-business|intra business|intra-organisational
questions.e: B2B covers dealings between firms, B2C covers firm-to-customer dealings, and intra-B covers transactions within the firm.

questions.t: Social Responsibility of Business and Business Ethics
questions.q: The obligation of a business to make decisions and act in ways that are desirable in terms of the values and objectives of society is called social ______.
questions.e: Social responsibility goes beyond legal duties and means business acting in the interest of society.

questions.t: Social Responsibility of Business and Business Ethics
questions.q: Paying taxes honestly and on time and respecting the laws of the land is the responsibility of business towards the ______.
questions.e: Business must function as a law-abiding citizen, paying taxes and dues honestly, as part of its responsibility to the government.

questions.t: Social Responsibility of Business and Business Ethics
questions.q: Without any legal requirement, a company in Chennai donates ₹10 lakh to a flood relief fund. Under the classification of social responsibility, this is ______ responsibility.
questions.e: Discretionary responsibility is purely voluntary, such as charity and helping in calamities.

questions.t: Social Responsibility of Business and Business Ethics
questions.q: A company avoids advertisements that hurt religious sentiments, even though no law prohibits them. This reflects ______ responsibility.
questions.e: Ethical responsibility covers behaviour that society expects but which is not required by law, like respecting religious sentiments in advertising.

questions.t: Social Responsibility of Business and Business Ethics
questions.q: Kapoor Textiles of Surat pays a fair dividend to its owners, provides safe working conditions to its staff, and sells good quality cloth at reasonable prices.
p: (a) Paying a fair return on investment is responsibility towards which group?
shareholders|owners|investors|shareholders or owners
(b) Providing safe working conditions is responsibility towards which group?
workers|employees|worker|employee
(c) Selling good quality goods at reasonable prices is responsibility towards which group?
consumers|customers|consumer|customer
questions.e: A business has responsibilities towards different interest groups: owners, workers, consumers, government and the community.

questions.q: Funds required for buying land, buildings and machinery are called ______ capital.
questions.e: Fixed capital requirements are for long-term assets, while working capital is needed for day-to-day operations.

questions.q: An instrument acknowledging a loan taken by a company, carrying a fixed rate of interest, is called a ______.
questions.e: Debentures are borrowed funds; debenture holders are creditors who get fixed interest regardless of profits.

questions.q: Shareholders who have voting rights, are the real owners of the company and get dividend only after preference shareholders hold ______ shares.
questions.e: Equity shareholders bear the highest risk, have voting rights and are paid dividend and capital last.

questions.q: An unsecured promissory note issued by large creditworthy companies to raise short-term funds is called ______.
questions.e: Commercial paper is a short-term unsecured money-market instrument issued at a discount by firms with high credit ratings.

questions.q: A shoe company buys leather worth ₹2,00,000 from a supplier and is allowed to pay after 60 days. Which source of short-term finance is used?
questions.e: Trade credit is credit extended by one trader to another when goods are bought without immediate payment.

questions.q: Shakti Ltd. issues 10,000 debentures of ₹100 each carrying 9% interest per annum.
p: (a) Calculate the annual interest payable (in ₹).
(b) Must this interest be paid even if the company suffers a loss? (yes/no)
yes
(c) Debenture holders are owners or creditors of the company?
creditors|creditor
questions.e: Interest = 10,000 × ₹100 × 9% = ₹90,000; debenture interest is a fixed charge payable even in a loss year because debenture holders are creditors.

questions.q: Which apex bank provides credit for agriculture as well as small, cottage and village industries in rural areas?
questions.a: nabard|national bank for agriculture and rural development
questions.e: NABARD was set up in 1982 to promote integrated rural development, including rural small industries.

questions.q: The bank set up as the principal financial institution for promotion, financing and development of small-scale industries in India is ______.
questions.a: sidbi|small industries development bank of india
questions.e: SIDBI provides direct and indirect financial assistance to the small-scale sector.

questions.q: Micro, small and medium enterprises in India are defined under the ______ Development Act, 2006.
questions.a: msmed|msme|micro small and medium enterprises|micro, small and medium enterprises
questions.e: The MSMED Act, 2006 classifies enterprises as micro, small or medium on the basis of investment (and now turnover).

questions.q: Sunita makes pickles at home in her village using family members as workers, simple tools and local raw materials. Such units are called ______ industries.
questions.e: Cottage (rural or traditional) industries are run by individuals with family labour, little capital and simple equipment, often at home.

questions.q: A trader who buys goods in bulk from manufacturers and sells them in smaller lots to retailers is a ______.
questions.e: Wholesalers link producers and retailers, buying in large quantities and selling in smaller lots.

questions.q: Large retail establishments with a number of departments under one roof, each specialising in a particular line of products, are called ______ stores.
questions.e: Departmental stores offer a wide variety of goods in separate departments under one roof and one management.

questions.q: From which date was the Goods and Services Tax (GST) introduced in India?
questions.e: GST, a destination-based single tax on supply of goods and services, came into force in India on 1 July 2017.

questions.q: Rohit notices that Bata shops in Delhi, Mumbai and Chennai look alike, sell the same products at the same prices and are controlled by a head office. Such shops are called multiple shops or ______ stores.
questions.e: Multiple shops or chain stores are branches of one organisation with uniform appearance, products and prices, centrally managed.

questions.q: Hari sells cheap toys and stationery every day on the pavement outside a school in Lucknow; he has no permanent shop. Among itinerant retailers, he is classified as a ______.
questions.a: street trader|street traders|pavement vendor|pavement vendors|street vendor|street vendors
questions.e: Street traders sit at busy places like footpaths and sell low-priced common-use goods; peddlers move door to door and market traders go to markets on fixed days.

questions.q: Buying goods from a foreign country is called ______.
questions.e: Import trade means purchasing goods from other countries; export means selling goods abroad.

questions.q: A Singapore firm imports crude rubber from Malaysia and, after light processing, exports it to European countries. This is called ______ trade.
questions.e: Entrepot trade means importing goods for the purpose of re-exporting them, often after some processing.

questions.q: An Indian exporter needs a document certifying that the goods were produced in India so that the importing country can grant tariff concessions. This document is the certificate of ______.
questions.e: A certificate of origin specifies the country of production and helps the importer claim tariff concessions.

questions.q: Sharma Exports of Tiruppur receives an order for cotton T-shirts from a buyer in the UK.
p: (a) The importer's bank sends a document guaranteeing payment to the exporter. Name it (letter of ______).
credit|letter of credit|lc
(b) The shipping company issues a document acknowledging receipt of goods on board the ship. Name it.
bill of lading|b/l|bl
(c) For India, is this an import or export transaction?
export|exports
questions.e: A letter of credit assures payment to the exporter; a bill of lading is the shipping company's receipt for goods on board, and selling abroad is export trade.

questions.q: Completing a task on time is effectiveness, while completing it with the minimum use of resources and cost is ______.
questions.e: Effectiveness is about achieving goals on time; efficiency is about doing the task with the least cost and resources.

questions.q: The force that binds all the other functions of management together is called the essence of management, or ______.
questions.e: Coordination synchronises the activities of different departments and runs through all functions of management.

questions.q: The CEO of Surya Ltd. decides to enter the rural market. The production head then prepares departmental plans and instructs supervisors to carry them out. The production head belongs to the ______ level of management.
questions.e: Middle-level managers (departmental heads) interpret top management's policies and assign duties to supervisors.

questions.q: Who is known as the father of general management?
questions.e: Henri Fayol, a French mining engineer, gave 14 general principles of management applicable to all organisations.

questions.q: How many principles of management were given by Henri Fayol?
questions.e: Fayol gave 14 principles, such as division of work, unity of command, unity of direction and scalar chain.

questions.q: Fayol's principle that each group of activities having the same objective must have one head and one plan is unity of ______.
questions.e: Unity of direction means one head and one plan for a group of activities with the same objective; it is different from unity of command.

questions.q: Taylor's wage technique that pays a higher rate per unit to workers who meet or exceed the standard output and a lower rate to those below it is called the ______ system.
questions.a: differential piece wage|differential piece wage system|differential piece rate|differential piece rate system
questions.e: The differential piece wage system distinguishes efficient from inefficient workers and motivates them to reach the standard.

questions.q: Under the differential piece wage system, the standard output is 10 units a day. Workers get ₹50 per unit if they meet the standard and ₹40 per unit if they do not. Arjun makes 11 units and Karan makes 9 units. How many rupees more does Arjun earn than Karan?
A manager at a Pune factory uses a stop-watch to determine the standard time taken by an average worker to complete each part of a job. Which technique of scientific management is this?
questions.e: Time study determines the standard time for a well-defined job, which helps fix a fair day's work and wages.

questions.q: In Sunrise Ltd., Ravi, a production supervisor, receives conflicting orders from both the marketing head and the finance head, and is confused about whom to obey.
p: (a) Which principle of Fayol is being violated?
unity of command
(b) Which technique of Taylor deliberately gives each worker several specialist bosses?
functional foremanship
(c) How many specialists are there under that technique?
questions.e: Fayol's unity of command says one subordinate should have only one boss; Taylor's functional foremanship separates planning and execution with 8 specialist foremen.

questions.q: Growing health awareness in Indian cities has increased the demand for organic food, green tea and fitness equipment. Which dimension of the business environment does this reflect?
questions.e: The social environment includes customs, values and lifestyle trends such as health consciousness, which create new opportunities.

questions.q: Maruti Udyog became the leader in the small car market because it was the first to recognise the need for small cars in India. This shows which importance of understanding the business environment?
questions.a: identifying opportunities and getting the first mover advantage
o: assisting in planning and policy formulation
questions.e: Understanding the environment enables a firm to identify opportunities early and gain the first mover advantage, as Maruti did.

questions.q: Under the New Economic Policy of 1991, the government of India abolished industrial licensing for most industries, sold part of its shareholding in public sector units, and reduced import duties.
p: (a) Abolishing industrial licensing is part of which policy?
liberalisation|liberalization
(b) Selling part of the government's shares in public sector units is part of which policy?
privatisation|privatization|disinvestment
(c) Reducing import duties to integrate with the world economy is part of which policy?
globalisation|globalization
questions.e: The 1991 reforms were built on liberalisation (freeing from controls), privatisation (greater role of private sector) and globalisation (integration with the world economy).

questions.q: A plan that states expected results in numerical terms, such as expected sales of ₹50 lakh in a year, is a ______.
questions.e: A budget is a statement of expected results expressed in numbers; it is both a plan and a control device.

questions.q: A specific statement that tells what must or must not be done, leaving no scope for discretion, such as 'No smoking inside the factory', is a ______.
questions.e: Rules are rigid and must be followed; violation usually leads to a penalty.

questions.q: A company decides that it will recruit only graduates for its junior management positions. This general guideline that sets the boundaries for decision-making is a ______.
questions.e: Policies are general statements that guide thinking and decision-making, such as a recruitment policy.

questions.q: ABC Ltd. wants to increase its sales by 10% this year. To face a rival's new product, it decides on a comprehensive plan of TV advertising and price cuts, keeping in mind that planning always deals with the future.
p: (a) The aim of increasing sales by 10% is which type of plan?
objective|objectives
(b) The comprehensive plan to deal with the rival's new product is which type of plan?
strategy|strategies
(c) Planning deals with the future. Which feature of planning is this? (planning is ______)
futuristic|future oriented|forward looking|future-oriented
questions.e: Objectives are end results; a strategy is a comprehensive plan to achieve objectives in view of the environment; planning is futuristic as it looks ahead.

questions.q: The grouping of similar activities into jobs and jobs into departments is called ______.
questions.e: Departmentalisation groups similar or related jobs into units like production, finance and marketing.

questions.q: In the delegation of authority, which element can never be delegated?
questions.e: Authority can be delegated, but accountability cannot; the superior remains answerable for the work delegated.

questions.q: The systematic delegation of authority to the lowest levels throughout the organisation is called ______.
questions.e: Decentralisation is the extension of delegation to all levels, giving lower levels decision-making power.

questions.q: A company makes cosmetics, garments and footwear, and sets up a separate unit with its own production, finance and marketing for each product. Which organisational structure is it using?
questions.e: A divisional structure groups activities by product lines, each division being responsible for its own profit or loss.

questions.q: The process of searching for prospective employees and stimulating them to apply for jobs is called ______.
questions.e: Recruitment builds a pool of applicants; selection then chooses the most suitable from them.

questions.q: Training in which employees learn on equipment similar to that used on the job, but in a separate area away from the actual workplace, is ______ training.
questions.e: Vestibule training is an off-the-job method used for costly or delicate equipment so that production is not disturbed.

questions.q: Recruitment is called a positive process, while selection is called a ______ process because it rejects many applicants.
questions.e: Selection eliminates unsuitable candidates at each stage, so it is considered a negative process.

questions.q: A bank fills a vacancy in its Jaipur branch by shifting an officer from its Kota branch at the same level and pay. Which internal source of recruitment is used?
questions.e: Transfer is the shifting of an employee from one job or place to another without change in responsibility or pay.

questions.q: How many levels of needs are there in Maslow's need hierarchy theory?
questions.e: Maslow's five needs are physiological, safety, belongingness, esteem and self-actualisation.

questions.q: According to Maslow, the need for affection, acceptance and friendship is the ______ need.
questions.e: Belongingness (social) needs come after safety needs and relate to affection, acceptance and friendship.

questions.q: The leadership style in which the leader gives orders and expects subordinates to obey them without question is ______ leadership.
questions.e: An autocratic leader centralises decision-making and uses one-way communication.

questions.q: Infosys offers its employees company shares at a price lower than the market price. Which financial incentive is this?
questions.a: co-partnership|co partnership|stock option|stock options|employee stock option|esop
questions.e: Co-partnership or stock options let employees own a part of the company, creating a sense of ownership.

questions.q: In Sharma Enterprises, a worker's complaint travels through the supervisor and manager to the director. Meanwhile, rumours of a bonus spread quickly through casual chats among workers. Some instructions are misunderstood because the words used have different meanings.
p: (a) Communication that follows the chain of command is which type?
formal|formal communication
(b) What is the informal communication network called?
grapevine
(c) Misunderstanding due to words with different meanings is which type of barrier?
semantic|semantic barrier|semantic barriers
questions.e: Formal communication flows through official channels; informal communication is called the grapevine; semantic barriers arise from problems in encoding and decoding messages.

questions.q: Controlling is both a forward looking and a ______ looking function.
questions.e: Controlling compares past performance with standards and also improves future performance.

questions.q: Planning and controlling are inseparable: planning without controlling is meaningless, and controlling without ______ is blind.
questions.e: Plans provide the standards for control, and control checks whether plans are being followed.

questions.q: In a Ludhiana factory, the standard output is 200 units per day but actual output is 180 units. The manager ignores a 1% rise in stationery expenses but takes action on the output shortfall.
p: (a) Calculate the percentage deviation in output.
(b) Attending only to significant deviations is called management by ______.
exception
(c) Focusing control on key result areas like output is called ______ control.
critical point|critical-point
questions.e: Deviation = (200 − 180)/200 × 100 = 10%; management by exception focuses on significant deviations, and critical point control focuses on key result areas.

questions.q: The decision regarding how much of the profit is to be distributed to shareholders and how much is to be retained is the ______ decision.
questions.e: The dividend decision divides earnings between dividends to shareholders and retained earnings.

questions.q: Long-term investment decisions, such as buying a new machine or opening a new plant, are also called ______ decisions.
questions.e: Capital budgeting decisions involve huge amounts, affect long-term growth and are irreversible except at a high cost.

questions.q: A company has EBIT of ₹5,00,000, 10% debentures of ₹10,00,000 and a tax rate of 30%. Calculate its profit after tax in ₹.

Vardhan Ltd. needs ₹50 lakh. Its expected return on investment is 15%, the tax rate is 30% and equity shares are of ₹10 each. Plan I: all equity (5,00,000 shares). Plan II: ₹25 lakh equity (2,50,000 shares) and ₹25 lakh 10% debt.
p: (a) Calculate EBIT in ₹.
(b) Calculate EPS under Plan I in ₹.
(c) Calculate EPS under Plan II in ₹.
questions.e: EBIT = 15% of ₹50 lakh = ₹7,50,000. Plan I: EAT = ₹5,25,000, EPS = ₹1.05. Plan II: interest ₹2,50,000, EBT ₹5,00,000, EAT ₹3,50,000, EPS = ₹1.40. EPS rises because ROI exceeds the cost of debt (trading on equity).

questions.q: The market in which securities are issued for the first time is the ______ market.
questions.e: The primary or new issue market deals with fresh securities; the secondary market deals with already-issued securities.

questions.q: The statutory body that regulates the securities market in India is ______.
questions.a: sebi|securities and exchange board of india
questions.e: SEBI, given statutory powers in 1992, protects investors and regulates and develops the securities market.

questions.q: The money market instrument issued by the RBI on behalf of the Government of India to meet short-term borrowing needs, with maturities like 91, 182 and 364 days, is the ______.
questions.e: Treasury bills are zero-coupon instruments issued at a discount and redeemed at par.

questions.q: Tata Steel offers new shares to its existing shareholders in proportion to the shares they already hold. This method of floatation is a ______.
questions.e: In a rights issue, existing shareholders get the privilege to buy new shares in proportion to their holdings.

questions.q: The four Ps of the marketing mix are product, price, place and ______.
questions.e: The marketing mix consists of product, price, place (physical distribution) and promotion.

questions.q: The marketing philosophy which holds that a firm should identify and satisfy customer needs better than its competitors is the ______ concept.
questions.e: The marketing concept starts with the customer's needs and aims at profit through customer satisfaction.

questions.q: A brand or part of a brand that is given legal protection so that no one else can use it is a ______.
questions.e: A registered trademark gives the firm exclusive legal right to use the brand name or mark.

questions.q: A shoe company sells its products to customers only through its own retail outlets, without any middlemen. Which channel of distribution is this?
questions.e: A zero-level or direct channel involves no intermediaries between manufacturer and consumer.

questions.q: Maya Foods launches a new mango juice. It distributes free sample sachets in markets, offers 'buy two, get one free', and gets favourable news stories about the juice published in newspapers. The juice comes in an attractive tetra pack that protects and promotes it.
p: (a) Free samples and 'buy two, get one free' are tools of which element of the promotion mix?
sales promotion
(b) Getting favourable news stories published is part of which element of the promotion mix?
public relations|publicity|pr
(c) Designing the container of the product is called ______.
packaging
questions.e: Sales promotion gives short-term incentives; public relations builds goodwill through publicity; packaging protects the product and helps promote it.

questions.q: In which year was the Consumer Protection Act currently in force in India passed?
questions.e: The Consumer Protection Act, 2019 replaced the Act of 1986.

questions.q: The quality certification mark of the Bureau of Indian Standards for industrial and consumer products like electrical appliances is the ______ mark.
questions.e: The ISI mark shows that a product conforms to the standards set by the Bureau of Indian Standards.

questions.q: The quality certification mark used for agricultural products like spices, honey and pulses is ______.
questions.e: Agmark certifies the quality of agricultural produce; FPO is for processed fruit products and Hallmark for gold jewellery.

questions.q: Kavita bought a mixer-grinder for ₹4,000 from a shop in Bhopal. It stopped working within a week, and the shopkeeper refused to replace it.
p: (a) Which consumer right does Kavita exercise by filing a complaint?
right to seek redressal|seek redressal|redressal|right to redressal
(b) Under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019, which commission should she approach?
district commission|district|district consumer disputes redressal commission
(c) An appeal against an order of the National Commission lies with which court?
supreme court|supreme court of india
questions.e: The right to seek redressal lets consumers get relief for defective goods; a claim of this size goes to the District Commission, and appeals against National Commission orders lie with the Supreme Court.

questions.q: Management is called a ______ process because its functions of planning, organising, staffing, directing and controlling are performed again and again.
questions.e: The functions of management form an ongoing series of interrelated activities.

questions.q: Management is said to be ______ because it is needed in all types of organisations: economic, social and political.
questions.e: Management is universal; it applies to businesses, schools, hospitals and governments alike.

questions.q: Management is ______ because it cannot be seen, but its presence is felt in the way the organisation functions.
questions.e: The effect of management shows in targets met, orderly work and satisfied employees.

questions.q: The chairman, chief executive officer and board of directors belong to the ______ level of management.
questions.e: Top management sets overall objectives and strategies and is responsible for the welfare and survival of the organisation.

questions.q: Foremen and supervisors belong to the ______ level of management.
questions.e: Supervisory or operational management directly oversees the efforts of the workforce.

questions.q: The function of management that compares actual performance with planned standards and takes corrective action is ______.
questions.e: Controlling ensures that organisational resources are used to achieve the planned goals.

questions.q: Management does not fully satisfy the features of a profession mainly because there is no restriction on ______ to it, unlike medicine or law.
questions.e: Anyone can be called a manager regardless of qualification, so management lacks restricted entry.

questions.q: Coordination is a ______ function because a manager has to make conscious efforts to coordinate the work of different people.
questions.e: Even where people cooperate willingly, coordination does not happen by itself; managers must plan it.

questions.q: Providing employment, supplying quality products and using environment-friendly methods of production are the ______ objectives of management.
questions.e: Social objectives involve creating benefit for society; organisational objectives are survival, profit and growth.

questions.q: Tasty Foods Ltd. aims first to earn enough revenue to cover its costs so that it can stay in business. Which organisational objective of management is this?
questions.e: Survival is the basic organisational objective; a business must at least cover its costs to stay in existence.

questions.q: Management has a systematised body of knowledge, but its principles are not as exact as those of physics because they deal with human behaviour. Management is therefore called an ______ science.
questions.e: Management principles must be modified to suit situations, so management is an inexact science.

questions.q: A manager applies management principles creatively and in a personalised way to suit each situation. This shows management as an ______.
questions.e: Art involves personalised, creative application of existing knowledge, which improves with practice.

questions.q: In Nirmal Ltd., the production manager produced the target of 1,000 units on time, but used far more raw material than necessary, raising the cost per unit.
p: (a) Which quality did the manager achieve by meeting the target on time?
effectiveness
(b) Which quality was missing because more resources were used?
efficiency
(c) At which level of management is the production manager?
middle|middle level
questions.e: Effectiveness is completing the job on time; efficiency is doing it at minimum cost. A departmental head such as the production manager is middle management.

questions.q: Who is known as the father of scientific management?
questions.a: taylor|f w taylor|frederick winslow taylor|frederick taylor|fw taylor
questions.e: F. W. Taylor developed scientific management to improve productivity in factories.

questions.q: Fayol's principle that there should be a place for everything and everyone, and everything and everyone should be in its place, is ______.
questions.e: Order ensures that people and materials are found in their proper places, saving time and effort.

questions.q: Fayol's principle stating that there should be a formal line of authority from the highest to the lowest ranks is the ______ chain.
questions.e: The scalar chain is the chain of superiors from top to bottom through which communication normally flows.

questions.q: In an emergency, Fayol allowed direct communication between employees at the same level, without going through the scalar chain. This is called a ______.
questions.e: The gang plank permits quick communication between equals while keeping superiors informed.

questions.q: The technique of scientific management that aims to eliminate unnecessary varieties, sizes and dimensions of products is ______.
questions.e: Simplification cuts out superfluous diversity, reducing inventory and cost.

questions.q: A manager stops treating employees differently on the basis of their religion and behaves with kindness and justice towards all. Which principle of Fayol is he following?
questions.e: Equity requires kindliness and justice towards workers, without discrimination on grounds such as religion, caste or gender.

questions.q: A factory studies movements of workers such as lifting, sitting and changing positions to eliminate unnecessary movements. Which technique of scientific management is this?
questions.e: Motion study identifies and removes unproductive movements so that a job takes less time.

questions.q: A company decides the frequency and length of rest intervals that workers need to restore their energy while doing a job. Which technique of scientific management is this?
questions.e: Fatigue study determines the amount and frequency of rest needed to complete a task.

questions.q: In Unity Ltd., the management shares the gains of higher productivity with the workers, and both sides give up their mistrust of each other. The workers also take pride in working as one team.
p: (a) Which principle of Taylor calls for complete harmony between management and workers?
harmony not discord|harmony, not discord
(b) The complete change in the attitude of both management and workers that Taylor called for is mental ______.
revolution
(c) Which principle of Fayol promotes team spirit and unity among employees?
esprit de corps
questions.e: Harmony, not discord requires mental revolution, a change of attitude on both sides; esprit de corps means union is strength.

questions.q: The business environment is the sum total of all individuals, institutions and other forces that are ______ the control of a business but may affect its performance.
questions.e: External forces such as customers, competitors, government and technology make up the business environment.

questions.q: In which year did the Government of India announce the New Economic Policy based on liberalisation, privatisation and globalisation?
questions.e: The New Economic Policy of July 1991 began major economic reforms in India.

questions.q: Interest rates, inflation, the stock market index and the disposable income of people are part of the ______ environment.
questions.e: Economic factors affect the demand for goods and the cost of doing business.

questions.q: Political stability and the attitude of the government towards business form part of the ______ environment.
questions.e: Political conditions affect business confidence and the policies governing business.

questions.q: The spread of digital payment apps that has reduced the use of cheques shows a change in the ______ environment.
questions.e: The technological environment includes new methods, products and ways of doing things.

questions.q: The business environment keeps changing because of changes in technology, consumer tastes and government policies. So it is ______ in nature.
questions.e: The business environment is dynamic, not static.

questions.q: The feature that the business environment differs from country to country and region to region is called ______.
questions.e: For example, the demand for a product may be high in one region and low in another.

questions.q: Positive external changes that a business can use to improve its performance are called ______.
questions.e: Understanding the environment helps a firm to identify opportunities and get the first mover advantage.

questions.q: External trends, such as the entry of a strong new competitor, that may hinder the performance of a business are called ______.
questions.e: Environmental scanning warns a firm about threats so that it can prepare for them.

questions.q: The Consumer Protection Act, 2019 and the Competition Act, 2002 are part of the ______ environment of business.
questions.e: The legal environment includes laws passed by the government and decisions of courts and commissions.

questions.q: Understanding the business environment helps a firm to identify threats in time. These are called early ______ signals.
questions.e: Early warning signals help a firm take timely steps to deal with threats.

questions.q: The Reserve Bank of India raises the repo rate, making car loans costlier and reducing car sales. Which dimension of the business environment does this reflect?
questions.e: Interest rates and monetary policy are part of the economic environment.

questions.q: The business environment includes specific forces, such as customers and competitors, and ______ forces, such as social, political and legal conditions.
questions.e: Specific forces affect individual firms directly; general forces affect all firms indirectly.

questions.q: Planning is the ______ function of management because all other functions are performed within the framework of plans.
questions.e: Planning lays down the base for organising, staffing, directing and controlling.

questions.q: Plans that are used again and again for recurring situations, such as policies, procedures and rules, are called ______ plans.
questions.e: Standing plans are used repeatedly; single-use plans, such as budgets for an event, are used once.

questions.q: Planning focuses on achieving the ______ of the organisation, and every plan must contribute to them.
questions.e: Planning is goal-oriented: plans are made to achieve the stated objectives.

questions.q: Planning is a ______ exercise because it requires foresight, logical thinking and sound judgement rather than guesswork.
questions.e: Planning is an intellectual activity of thinking before doing.

questions.q: A plan that lays down the steps to be followed in a fixed chronological order for routine activities, such as issuing materials from the store, is a ______.
questions.e: Procedures specify the exact sequence of steps for doing routine work.

questions.q: A plan that prescribes the way or manner in which a particular task is to be performed, such as a training technique, is a ______.
questions.e: Methods are the prescribed ways of doing a task; the best method saves time and effort.

questions.q: A detailed statement about a project that outlines its objectives, policies, procedures, rules, tasks and resources, such as launching a new product, is a ______.
questions.e: Programmes combine plans, budgets and procedures for a particular project.

questions.q: Planning involves choosing the best course of action from among several alternatives, so it involves ______ making.
questions.e: Planning is essentially decision-making, because it means selecting among alternatives.

questions.q: In the planning process, the step that comes immediately after setting objectives is developing ______.
questions.e: Planning premises are assumptions about the future, such as expected demand, on which plans are based.

questions.q: After identifying alternative courses of action, the next step in the planning process is ______ the alternatives.
questions.e: Each alternative is weighed for its positive and negative points before one is selected.

questions.q: The last step in the planning process, which checks whether plans are being carried out as intended, is ______ action.
questions.e: Follow-up action monitors the plans to ensure that objectives are achieved.

questions.q: A company spends many weeks collecting facts and testing alternatives before finalising a plan, delaying action. This limitation of planning is that it is time-______.
questions.e: Planning takes time, and sometimes not much time is left for implementation.

questions.q: The first step in the process of organising is identification and ______ of work.
questions.e: The total work is divided into manageable activities to avoid duplication and share the burden.

questions.q: The organisational structure in which activities are grouped by functions such as production, purchase, marketing and finance is the ______ structure.
questions.e: A functional structure groups jobs of a similar nature into functional departments.

questions.q: The number of subordinates that a superior can effectively manage is called the span of ______.
questions.e: The span of management determines the number of levels in the organisation.

questions.q: Informal organisation arises from the ______ interaction of people working together in an organisation.
questions.e: Informal groups form on the basis of common interests, tastes and friendships.

questions.q: In an organisation, authority flows ______ from superior to subordinate.
questions.e: Authority flows downward, while responsibility and accountability flow upward.

questions.q: Delegation is compulsory in every organisation, whereas decentralisation is an ______ policy decision of top management.
questions.e: No manager can do all the work alone, so delegation is necessary; decentralisation is a matter of choice.

questions.q: The obligation of a subordinate to properly perform the duty assigned to him is called ______.
questions.e: Responsibility arises from the superior-subordinate relationship and flows upward.

questions.q: In the organising process, deciding who reports to whom, such as the finance manager reporting to the general manager, is the step of establishing ______ relationships.
questions.e: Clear reporting relationships create a hierarchy and help coordination.

questions.q: A company has a separate production, finance and marketing team in each of its product divisions. This leads to duplication of effort, a disadvantage of the ______ structure.
questions.e: In a divisional structure each division has its own functions, so resources may be duplicated.

questions.q: Informal organisation helps information to spread quickly, but one of its disadvantages is that it can spread ______.
questions.e: The informal network may carry rumours, which can work against the organisation.

questions.q: A sales manager allows a salesperson to give discounts of up to 10%, but the sales manager remains answerable to the general manager for the results. This answerability is called ______.
questions.e: Accountability cannot be delegated; the sales manager is still answerable for the final outcome.

questions.q: Delta Ltd. groups its work into production, finance, marketing and human resources departments, each headed by a manager reporting to the CEO. Authority is systematically passed down to the lowest levels. Employees who share an interest in cricket have also formed their own club.
p: (a) Which organisational structure does Delta Ltd. follow?
functional|functional structure
(b) The systematic delegation of authority to the lowest levels is called ______.
decentralisation|decentralization
(c) The cricket club formed by employees is an example of which type of organisation?
informal|informal organisation|informal organization
questions.e: Grouping by function is a functional structure; delegation to all levels is decentralisation; groups formed by shared interests are informal organisations.

questions.q: The managerial function of filling and keeping filled the positions in the organisation structure is ______.
questions.e: Staffing puts the right people in the right jobs.

questions.q: The first step in the staffing process is estimating the ______ requirement of the organisation.
questions.e: Workload analysis and workforce analysis show how many and what type of people are needed.

questions.q: Filling vacancies from within the organisation, through promotion or transfer, is ______ recruitment.
questions.e: Internal sources motivate existing employees and are economical.

questions.q: Training under a joint programme of an educational institution and a business firm, in which selected students work in the firm, is ______ training.
questions.e: Internship training gives students practical knowledge along with theory.

questions.q: Training in which a trainee works under the guidance of a master worker for a prescribed period, as in plumbing or electrical work, is ______ training.
questions.e: Apprenticeship programmes are used for jobs that need a long period of practice.

questions.q: Introducing a newly selected employee to his colleagues and familiarising him with the rules and policies of the organisation is called ______.
questions.e: Orientation helps a new employee settle into the organisation.

questions.q: Training is job-oriented, whereas ______ is career-oriented and aims at the overall growth of an employee.
questions.e: Training improves skills for a particular job; development prepares employees for higher responsibilities.

questions.q: A company hires top executives through firms that maintain a database of qualified candidates and charge a fee for their services. Which source of recruitment is this?
questions.e: Placement agencies and management consultants screen candidates and recommend suitable names to employers.

questions.q: A factory puts up a notice on its gate stating the details of vacancies for unskilled workers, and job-seekers assemble there on the given date. Which source of recruitment is this?
questions.e: Direct recruitment is used for casual or unskilled jobs and costs very little.

questions.q: A selection test that measures an individual's potential for learning new skills is the ______ test.
questions.e: Aptitude tests indicate a person's capacity to develop with training.

questions.q: A selection test that measures the existing skills and knowledge of a candidate in a particular area of work is the ______ test.
questions.e: Trade tests distinguish between the knowledge and skill a candidate already has and the potential to acquire it.

questions.q: Raman Industries needs 20 machine operators. It invites job-seekers registered with government employment exchanges, selects candidates after tests and interviews, puts each selected person on the job for which he was chosen, and then trains them on dummy machines in a separate area away from the factory floor.
p: (a) Which source of recruitment is used?
employment exchange|employment exchanges
(b) Putting a selected candidate on the job for which he has been selected is called ______.
placement
(c) Training on dummy machines away from the actual work floor is which type of training?
vestibule|vestibule training
questions.e: Employment exchanges are an external source; placement is the step after selection; vestibule training uses equipment similar to the real job in a separate area.

questions.q: The process of stimulating people to act to achieve desired goals is called ______.
questions.e: Motivation depends on satisfying people's needs.

questions.q: According to Maslow, the most basic needs, such as food, water and shelter, are ______ needs.
questions.e: Physiological needs are at the base of Maslow's hierarchy.

questions.q: The leadership style in which the leader gives subordinates complete freedom to make decisions is ______ leadership.
questions.e: A laissez-faire leader uses little power and acts mainly as a support to the group.

questions.q: According to Maslow, the highest-level need, to become what one is capable of becoming, is the ______ need.
questions.e: Self-actualisation includes growth, self-fulfilment and achievement of goals.

questions.q: A leader who consults subordinates and encourages them to take part in decision-making follows the ______ style of leadership.
questions.e: A democratic leader develops action plans in consultation with subordinates.

questions.q: Overseeing the work of subordinates at the operative level by a superior is called ______.
questions.e: Supervision ensures that work is done as per instructions and maintains discipline.

questions.q: Job security, a stable income and pension plans satisfy ______ needs in Maslow's hierarchy.
questions.e: Safety or security needs provide protection from physical and emotional harm.

questions.q: Ramesh is given a higher designation and a bigger cabin, without any increase in pay. Which non-financial incentive is used?
questions.e: Status refers to the ranking of positions; a higher status satisfies esteem needs.

questions.q: A company redesigns jobs to include greater variety of work, more autonomy and opportunities for personal growth. Which non-financial incentive is this?
questions.e: Job enrichment makes jobs more interesting and challenging.

questions.q: An employee misses important parts of a message because he is preoccupied with personal problems and does not pay attention. Which type of communication barrier is this?
questions.e: Psychological barriers include lack of attention, premature evaluation, loss by transmission and distrust.

questions.q: In a large company, rigid rules and too many levels in the hierarchy delay messages and distort them. Which type of communication barrier is this?
questions.e: Organisational barriers arise from policies, rules, status and a complex organisation structure.

questions.q: The first step in the process of controlling is setting performance ______.
questions.e: Standards are the criteria against which actual performance is measured.

questions.q: Comparing actual performance with the standards set helps a manager to find ______.
questions.e: Deviations are the differences between actual and planned performance.

questions.q: The final step in the controlling process is taking ______ action.
questions.e: Corrective action brings performance back in line with the standards.

questions.q: Checking actual results by personal observation, sample checking or performance reports is the step of ______ of actual performance.
questions.e: Performance should be measured in the same units as the standards.

questions.q: Employees work harder when they know their performance will be judged against standards. So a good control system improves employee ______.
questions.e: Controlling motivates employees and helps them give better performance.

questions.q: A limitation of controlling is that a company has little control over ______ factors such as government policies and changes in technology.
questions.e: An organisation cannot control external factors such as competition and policy changes.

questions.q: Controlling becomes difficult where standards cannot be set in quantitative terms, for example for employee ______ and human behaviour.
questions.e: Qualitative factors such as morale are difficult to measure and control.

questions.q: Controlling is a ______ function because it is performed by managers at all levels and in all types of organisations.
questions.e: Every manager has to monitor and control the work under him.

questions.q: The standard cost of production of a product is ₹500 per unit but the actual cost is ₹540 per unit. Calculate the percentage deviation.
A sales target was set at 1,000 units, but actual sales were 1,150 units. Calculate the percentage deviation from the target.
Finding the causes of significant deviations, such as defective machinery or poor raw material, comes under the step of ______ deviations.
questions.e: Analysing deviations helps identify their causes so that the right corrective action can be taken.

questions.q: Controlling is a costly affair, so a small firm should introduce an elaborate control system only if its ______ are greater than its costs.
questions.e: The benefits of a control system must outweigh the cost of installing and running it.

questions.q: A company finds that a deviation arose because the standard itself was set too high to be achieved. The corrective action is to ______ the standard.
questions.e: If standards are unrealistic, they should be revised.

questions.q: The decision about how much finance is to be raised from various long-term sources, such as shares and debt, is the ______ decision.
questions.e: The financing decision determines the capital structure of the company.

questions.q: The proportion of debt and equity used by a company to finance its business is called its capital ______.
questions.e: Capital structure refers to the mix between owners' funds and borrowed funds.

questions.q: The capital required to meet the day-to-day operations of a business, such as buying raw materials, is ______ capital.
questions.e: Working capital is invested in current assets.

questions.q: Using fixed-cost debt to increase the earnings per share of equity shareholders is called trading on ______.
questions.e: Trading on equity is favourable when the return on investment is higher than the rate of interest on debt.

questions.q: Estimating the fund requirements of a business and specifying the sources of those funds is called financial ______.
questions.e: Financial planning ensures that funds are available when needed and that funds are not raised unnecessarily.

questions.q: A business with a long operating cycle needs ______ working capital.
questions.e: The longer the operating cycle, the larger the amount of working capital required.

questions.q: A trading concern usually needs ______ fixed capital than a manufacturing concern.
questions.e: A trading concern does not need plant and machinery, so its fixed capital needs are lower.

questions.q: Debt is generally a ______ source of finance than equity because interest is a tax-deductible expense.
questions.e: The cost of debt is lower because the lender's risk is lower and interest reduces taxable income.

questions.q: A company has EBIT of ₹4,00,000 and an annual interest charge of ₹80,000. Calculate its interest coverage ratio.
questions.e: Interest coverage ratio = EBIT ÷ Interest = 4,00,000 ÷ 80,000 = 5 times.

questions.q: A company has EBIT of ₹6,00,000, 12% debentures of ₹20,00,000, a tax rate of 30% and 1,00,000 equity shares. Calculate its EPS in ₹.
A company's return on investment is lower than the rate of interest on debt. To avoid a fall in EPS, it should use ______ debt in its capital structure.
questions.e: Trading on equity is unfavourable when ROI is below the cost of debt, so debt should be reduced.

questions.q: A company with stable earnings over the years is in a position to declare ______ dividends.
questions.e: Stability of earnings is a factor affecting the dividend decision; stable earnings allow higher dividends.

questions.q: The market for short-term funds, with a maturity of up to one year, is the ______ market.
questions.e: The money market deals in instruments such as treasury bills, commercial paper and call money.

questions.q: An unsecured promissory note issued by a firm to raise short-term funds is called a commercial ______.
questions.e: Commercial paper is a short-term, negotiable instrument with a fixed maturity.

questions.q: Call money is short-term finance repayable on demand, with a maturity period ranging from one day to ______ days.
questions.e: Call money is used mainly by banks for inter-bank transactions.

questions.q: Commercial paper is issued for a maturity period ranging from 15 days to ______ year.
questions.e: Commercial paper is a short-term money market instrument with a maximum maturity of one year.

questions.q: Certificates of deposit are unsecured, negotiable, short-term instruments in bearer form, issued by commercial banks and development ______ institutions.
questions.e: Certificates of deposit are issued to individuals, corporations and companies during periods of tight liquidity.

questions.q: A bill of exchange drawn by a seller on a buyer, used to finance the working capital needs of firms, is a ______ bill.
questions.e: A commercial bill can be discounted with a bank before maturity.

questions.q: In the method of floatation in which securities are first sold to intermediaries such as issuing houses, who then resell them to the public, the method is offer for ______.
questions.e: In an offer for sale, the issuing company does not sell directly to the public.

questions.q: A company sells its securities to institutional investors and selected individuals rather than to the general public. Which method of floatation is this?
questions.e: Private placement saves the cost of a public issue.

questions.q: A company issues its shares to the public through the online system of a stock exchange. Which method of floatation is this?
questions.a: e-ipo|eipo|e ipo|electronic initial public offer|electronic ipo
questions.e: In an e-IPO, the company enters into an agreement with the stock exchange to issue capital through its online system.

questions.q: Prohibiting fraudulent and unfair trade practices and insider trading are ______ functions of SEBI.
questions.e: SEBI's protective functions safeguard the interests of investors.

questions.q: Registration of brokers, sub-brokers and merchant bankers and regulating their working are ______ functions of SEBI.
questions.e: SEBI's regulatory functions frame rules for and control market intermediaries.

questions.q: The Securities and Exchange Board of India was first set up as an interim administrative body and later given statutory powers. It also runs programmes to train intermediaries and educate investors.
p: (a) In which year was SEBI set up?
(b) In which year was SEBI given statutory powers?
(c) Training intermediaries and educating investors are which type of functions of SEBI?
developmental|development|developmental functions
questions.e: SEBI was set up in 1988 and became a statutory body in 1992; training and investor education are its developmental functions.

questions.q: A name, term, sign, symbol or design used to identify the products of one seller and distinguish them from those of competitors is a ______.
questions.e: Branding helps in product differentiation and building customer loyalty.

questions.q: The information printed on a package that describes the product, its contents and how to use it is called a ______.
questions.e: Labels describe and identify the product and may also help promote it.

questions.q: Advertising is an ______ form of communication paid for by an identified sponsor.
questions.e: Advertising reaches a large audience without direct face-to-face contact.

questions.q: An oral presentation made in a conversation with prospective customers for the purpose of making sales is ______ selling.
questions.e: Personal selling is a two-way, face-to-face form of communication.

questions.q: The immediate container of a product, such as the bottle holding a shampoo, is ______ packaging.
questions.e: Primary packaging stays with the product until it is used.

questions.q: The marketing philosophy that customers prefer products that are widely available and inexpensive, so that firms should focus on efficient production, is the ______ concept.
questions.e: The production concept concentrates on improving production efficiency and reducing cost.

questions.q: The ______ marketing concept stresses customer satisfaction together with the long-term welfare of society.
questions.e: The societal marketing concept also considers social and environmental issues.

questions.q: A company promotes its product aggressively because it believes that customers will not buy enough of it unless they are persuaded. Which marketing philosophy is this?
questions.e: The selling concept focuses on aggressive selling and promotion.

questions.q: The main components of physical distribution are order processing, transportation, warehousing and ______ control.
questions.e: Inventory control decides how much stock to keep to meet demand at a reasonable cost.

questions.q: The element of the marketing mix concerned with making products available to customers where and when they want them is ______.
questions.e: Place covers channels of distribution and physical distribution of goods.

questions.q: A company believes that customers will favour products that offer the best quality, performance and features, and so it concentrates on improving its products. Which marketing philosophy is this?
questions.e: The product concept focuses on product quality and improvement.

questions.q: The consumer right to be protected against the marketing of goods that are hazardous to life and health is the right to ______.
questions.e: For example, electrical appliances with poor-quality parts can cause serious injury.

questions.q: The consumer right to choose from a variety of products at competitive prices is the right to ______.
questions.e: Marketers should offer a wide variety of products in terms of quality, brand, price and size.

questions.q: The quality certification mark used for gold jewellery is the ______.
questions.e: Hallmark certifies the purity of gold and silver jewellery.

questions.q: A consumer has the right to know the quality, quantity, purity, standard and price of a product. This is the right to be ______.
questions.e: Under the right to be informed, packages must carry details such as MRP, date of manufacture and ingredients.

questions.q: The right to acquire knowledge and skills needed to be a well-informed consumer throughout life is the right to consumer ______.
questions.e: Consumer education makes people aware of their rights and how to use them.

questions.q: The consumer right to file a complaint and have it considered in an appropriate forum is the right to be ______.
questions.e: The right to be heard allows consumers to voice their grievances.

questions.q: The quality certification mark for processed fruit products such as jams, squashes and pickles is ______.
questions.e: The FPO mark is issued for processed fruit products.

questions.q: Ravi buys a packet of biscuits on which the maximum retail price and the expiry date are not printed. Which consumer right is violated?
questions.e: The right to be informed entitles consumers to complete information about the product.

questions.q: Under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019, an appeal against an order of the District Commission lies with the ______ Commission.
questions.e: Appeals go from the District Commission to the State Commission, then to the National Commission and finally to the Supreme Court.

questions.q: As a responsible consumer, Meena insists on getting a ______ for every purchase so that she can file a complaint if needed.
questions.e: A cash memo is proof of purchase and is needed to support a complaint.

questions.q: Under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019, a complaint can be filed not only by a consumer but also by any registered voluntary consumer ______.
questions.e: Registered consumer associations, the Central or State Government and the Central Consumer Protection Authority may also file complaints.

questions.q: If the Commission is satisfied that the goods sold were defective, it may direct the seller to remove the defect, replace the goods or ______ the price paid.
questions.e: The reliefs available include removal of defects, replacement, refund of price and compensation.
